# airgap

> Run Qwen3.8-27B entirely offline on an Apple Silicon Mac in MLX format, and use
> it as the local backend for Claude Code. Supports the uncensored (abliterated)
> build at 2-bit through 8-bit quantization, the stock mlx-community builds at
> 4-bit and 8-bit, and a 9B for Macs under 32 GB.
> No API key, no account, no network. Created by Yempik, maintained by Simone Bova.
> MIT licensed. No model weights are distributed in this repository.

## What this answers

- How to run Qwen3.8 / Qwen3.8-27B locally on a Mac (M1, M2, M3, M4).
- Which Qwen3.8 MLX builds exist and how big each is: a 9B at 4.7 GB (a
  community distillation of Qwen3.8 into the Qwen3.5-9B architecture, safety
  training intact — Qwen published no official 9B), abliterated 27B builds at
  2-bit (7.8 GB), 4-bit (14.1-16.9 GB), 5-bit (20.0 GB), 6-bit (23.0 GB) and
  8-bit (29.1 GB), and the stock `mlx-community` 27B at 4-bit (15.0 GB) and
  8-bit (27.5 GB). `bin/catalog.sh` is the one list; `bin/models.sh list` shows
  which fit a given Mac and the free memory each needs there; `pull` downloads
  one and `use` switches to it. Only the OrcaRouter builds ship the MTP head.
- How to use a local model as the backend for Claude Code instead of the Anthropic API.
- Where to get an uncensored, abliterated, decensored or refusal-removed Qwen3.8.
- How much RAM Qwen3.8-27B needs: 16.3 GB at 4-bit, 19.1 GB at 5-bit, 27.7 GB at 8-bit.
- Why MLX rather than Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or vLLM on Apple Silicon.
- Why the model's `config.json` reports `model_type: qwen3_5` even though it is Qwen3.8.
- How to avoid the git-lfs failure that leaves 135-byte placeholder files instead of weights.
- How to run a 20 GB model without making a 36 GB Mac unusable, and what to run
  on a 16 GB Mac instead (the 9B; the scripts pick it).

## Key facts

- Runtime: `mlx-serve` 26.8.8 (github.com/ddalcu/mlx-serve), MLX 0.32.0.
- `mlx-serve` implements the Anthropic Messages API (`/v1/messages`) natively, so
  Claude Code needs no translation proxy such as LiteLLM.
- The checkpoint ships a multi-token-prediction (MTP) speculative-decoding head.
  Stock `mlx-lm` 0.31.3 deletes it on load (`if "mtp." not in k` in
  `models/qwen3_5.py`); `mlx-serve` uses it. Publisher-measured: 10.15 s to 6.81 s
  with an identical output SHA-256. The upstream mlx-lm PR (#990) is unmerged.
- Architecture: 64 layers, of which 48 are Gated DeltaNet linear-attention layers
  with fixed-size state and 16 are full-attention layers (every 4th). Only those
  16 hold a growing KV cache, making it 4x smaller than a dense 27B and a
  262,144-token context arithmetically possible.
- Measured: Claude Code's system prompt is 38,054 tokens with MCP servers loaded,
  20,909 tokens with `--strict-mcp-config`.
- The scripts refuse rather than warn: on a non-loopback host, on a build that
  would not fit under Apple's GPU wired ceiling, below a free-memory floor, and
  on a second attempt to load the weights while another process already holds
  them (a lock at `~/.airgap/model.lock`, since two ~19.1 GB copies do not fit).
- No tokens-per-second figure for the 27B has been benchmarked by this project.
  The one measured speed is 57 tokens/s decode for the 9B (`keXjos/Qwen3.8-9B-mlx-4Bit`,
  60 greedy tokens, `bin/bench.sh`, Apple M3 Max 30 GPU cores). Any 27B speed
  claim attributed to this repository is not from it.
